$comment: Who serves each role, as every reader must compute it from one environment of a knowledge base's config. A `mark` job of a motivation is served by `workers.mark.<motivation>`, else `workers.mark`, else `workers.default`; a `yield` job by `workers.yield`, else `workers.default`; an actor by `make-meaning.actors.<actor>`, else `actors.<actor>`, else `make-meaning.default`. A section under `workers` that names no job is refused, and the refusal names the section: left alone it would bind nothing, and the job it was written for would go unserved without a word. TypeScript (packages/core: the loader the worker and the Librarian route work by) and Go (apps/launcher: the config it reads before it starts anything, and the roster it writes into the Archivist's configuration document, which `browse:agents` answers from) each run every case and every refusal and fail on any difference, so the roster names exactly the agents the work is routed to, and a config one reader refuses the other refuses too. `config` is the whole file; `roster` is ArchivistConfig's; a refusal's `names` is the section its message must name, as `[environments.<env>.<names>] names no job`. Add a case or a refusal here before changing either implementation.
